findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~835 (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key / value_from_cursor) — The class drops DateTimePaginator's datetime↔epoch conversions: math.floor/math.ceil are applied directly to the field value (a datetime for order_by="-datetime"), raising TypeError, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor int so build_queryset filters the datetime column against an integer, making the paginator non-functional for the only endpoint it's wired to.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~870 (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, negative-offset branch) — Django QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported") for negative bounds; the comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false, so the enable_advanced_features path produces a 500 whenever a negative-offset cursor is used.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~73 — organization_context is not defined anywhere in this method (the endpoint receives organization and uses request.access), and enable_advanced is evaluated unconditionally before the use_optimized check, so every GET on this endpoint raises NameError and 500s; the lookup should also be moved inside the branch.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~180 (BasePaginator.get_result) — The new max(0, offset) clamp applies only to non-prev cursors, so prev cursors with a client-supplied negative offset still hit queryset[offset:stop] and raise AssertionError, contradicting the added safety comment; for forward cursors, negative offsets are silently clamped to 0, changing behavior of every endpoint sharing this paginator instead of rejecting the bad cursor.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py + src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua — No migration/cutover for the set→zset conversion: existing span-buf:s:* keys are plain sets, and the new zadd/zcard/zunionstore/zscan calls all raise WRONGTYPE against them; a rolling deploy also mixes old-version sadd writers with new zset readers, so batches fail until keys age out with no flush/migration strategy.

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~50 — zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MAX, so the default SUM aggregation corrupts scores whenever a member exists in both source keys (possible via at-least-once redelivery or a redirect chain resolving back to the span itself), doubling/garbling end_timestamp_precise and skewing eviction order; should use AGGREGATE MAX.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:~195 / add-buffer.lua — Removing the flush-time max_segment_spans check leaves the bulk-insert path unbounded: the Lua eviction runs during per-span evals (based on the pre-batch zcard/union count) before the batch's payloads are bulk-zadded, so a single batch containing a root plus >1000 children creates and flushes a segment over the cap with no enforcement anywhere.

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~63 — The eviction cap is hardcoded to 1000 while the existing configurable max_segment_spans option (orphaned by the removed flush-side check) is silently ignored, so deployments tuned to a different limit get data loss at 1000 regardless and the limit is no longer operator-configurable.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — The redirect-depth limit is silently cut from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") is deleted; trees deeper than 1000 redirects now silently fail to join, an undocumented behavior change.

[Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~65 — zpopmin eviction drops spans with no metric or log line, while the removed flush-side path emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded plus a logger.error; the new data loss is silent and unobservable in dashboards.

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~69 — The undocumented optimized_pagination query parameter makes one public endpoint return different pagination semantics and cursor formats depending on a hidden client param plus the caller's role; cursors generated by one paginator replayed against the other (param toggled between pages, or role/permission changing mid-session) produce broken or duplicated results, with no API documentation.

[Medium/api] PR scope — Large, unrelated, and non-functional changes to core audit-log pagination and BasePaginator are bundled into a PR titled as a spans-buffer optimization, and their comments make false safety claims ("permissions are checked at the queryset level", "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing"); these should be split out or reverted and reviewed separately.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator, the new endpoint branch/role gating, negative-offset behavior, or the BasePaginator.get_result change — the entire new pagination surface ships untested.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/ — No tests cover the new Lua behavior (eviction above 1000, zunionstore score aggregation with duplicate members, set→zset cutover); the only test changes add end_timestamp_precise literals, so eviction ordering and score handling are unverified.

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment claims Cursor now "allows negative offsets" as an optimization, but no functional change was made to the class; it documents behavior that doesn't exist (and negative offsets actually break queryset slicing downstream).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py + src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua — No migration/cutover for the set→zset conversion: existing span-buf:s:* keys are plain sets, and the new zadd/zcard/zunionstore/zscan calls all raise WRONGTYPE against them; a rolling deploy also mixes old-version sadd writers with new zset readers, so batches fail until keys age out with no flush/migration strategy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data type for span-buf:s:{...}:* keys from Set to ZSet: in buffer.py `p.sadd(...)` becomes `p.zadd(...)`, and reads change from `sscan` to `zscan`; the Lua script similarly switches `scard/sunionstore` to `zcard/zunionstore`. Redis will raise `WRONGTYPE` if existing keys are still Sets when `zadd/zscan/zcard` are used, and during a rolling deploy old code would still `SADD` into keys that new code expects to be ZSets (or vice versa), causing failures. The diff shows no migration, dual-read/write compatibility, or cutover strategy to handle existing set-typed keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~50 — zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MAX, so the default SUM aggregation corrupts scores whenever a member exists in both source keys (possible via at-least-once redelivery or a redirect chain resolving back to the span itself), doubling/garbling end_timestamp_precise and skewing eviction order; should use AGGREGATE MAX.

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the diff replaces set unions with `zunionstore` (e.g. `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` and similarly with `parent_key`) but does not specify an `AGGREGATE` mode. Redis defaults `ZUNIONSTORE` aggregation to `SUM`, so if the same member (span payload) exists in both source sorted sets, the resulting score will be summed. Given the Python side now stores spans in a ZSET with `end_timestamp_precise` as the score (`zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`), summing would corrupt timestamps and can skew eviction order used by `zpopmin` later in the script. The finding’s suggested fix (use `AGGREGATE MAX`) is grounded in this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:~195 / add-buffer.lua — Removing the flush-time max_segment_spans check leaves the bulk-insert path unbounded: the Lua eviction runs during per-span evals (based on the pre-batch zcard/union count) before the batch's payloads are bulk-zadded, so a single batch containing a root plus >1000 children creates and flushes a segment over the cap with no enforcement anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the only explicit span-count enforcement during flush: in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` guard is deleted, and the new zset-based loader only checks byte size while extending payloads from `zscan` results. At ingest time, `SpansBuffer.process_spans` now bulk-`ZADD`s all spans in a subsegment (`p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`) with no cap. The new eviction logic in `add-buffer.lua` (zcard/zunionstore + `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`) only runs when that Lua script is used; nothing in this diff shows `process_spans` invoking it, so a single batch can create a zset segment with >1000 members and there is no enforcement “anywhere” on the bulk path. This matches the finding’s scenario of an oversized segment being created/flushed without a count cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~63 — The eviction cap is hardcoded to 1000 while the existing configurable max_segment_spans option (orphaned by the removed flush-side check) is silently ignored, so deployments tuned to a different limit get data loss at 1000 regardless and the limit is no longer operator-configurable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a hard cap of 1000 in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (`if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin(..., span_count - 1000) end`), which will evict spans beyond 1000 unconditionally. At the same time, the Python flush-side enforcement that previously used `self.max_segment_spans` in `_load_segment_data` is removed (the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` branch is deleted), so the only visible span-count limiting is now this hardcoded 1000. This makes the previous configurable limit effectively ignored and can cause silent truncation/data loss at 1000 spans per segment regardless of deployment tuning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — The redirect-depth limit is silently cut from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") is deleted; trees deeper than 1000 redirects now silently fail to join, an undocumented behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the redirect traversal loop in `add-buffer.lua` from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explicit warning comment about depth-10k trees) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes that explanatory comment. There is also no new handling/logging if the loop hits the limit without resolving redirects, so the behavior change is silent. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that depths >1000 occur or that this concretely breaks correctness in practice, so it’s better framed as an undocumented/unguarded behavior change rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~65 — zpopmin eviction drops spans with no metric or log line, while the removed flush-side path emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded plus a logger.error; the new data loss is silent and unobservable in dashboards.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the new logic caps each sorted set at 1000 members by doing `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` when `span_count > 1000`, which irrevocably drops spans. The diff shows no accompanying `metrics.incr(...)` or `logger.error(...)` in this new eviction path. At the same time, the prior flush-side span-count guard in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py::_load_segment_data` that emitted `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` and a `logger.error(...)` is removed. Net result: span loss due to the new cap becomes silent/unobservable, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~69 — The undocumented optimized_pagination query parameter makes one public endpoint return different pagination semantics and cursor formats depending on a hidden client param plus the caller's role; cursors generated by one paginator replayed against the other (param toggled between pages, or role/permission changing mid-session) produce broken or duplicated results, with no API documentation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, undocumented `optimized_pagination=true` query param that conditionally switches the paginator class on the same endpoint (`DateTimePaginator` vs new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`) based on both the param and caller role (`is_superuser` or `has_global_access`). This makes the endpoint’s pagination behavior depend on a hidden client flag and permissions (see the new `use_optimized` / `enable_advanced` branch in `organization_auditlogs.py`). While the claim that cursors will definitively “replay” as broken/duplicated across paginators isn’t directly provable from the diff alone, the diff clearly introduces two different pagination implementations behind one endpoint without any guard to ensure cursor compatibility or API documentation, which is a concrete API/behavior consistency concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] PR scope — Large, unrelated, and non-functional changes to core audit-log pagination and BasePaginator are bundled into a PR titled as a spans-buffer optimization, and their comments make false safety claims ("permissions are checked at the queryset level", "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing"); these should be split out or reverted and reviewed separately.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces logic that can perform negative slicing on Django QuerySets. In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, both the modified existing paginator path (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` explicitly allow `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0`, leading to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices/offsets and will raise at runtime, contradicting the added comments claiming it is "safe" / "properly handles negative slicing". This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior change that can break pagination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator, the new endpoint branch/role gating, negative-offset behavior, or the BasePaginator.get_result change — the entire new pagination surface ships untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new pagination surface area without any corresponding test changes: (1) a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class in `sentry/api/paginator.py` with special negative-offset handling and cursor logic; (2) a new conditional branch in `organization_auditlogs.py` gated by `optimized_pagination=true` plus `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`; and (3) changes to `BasePaginator.get_result` slice start/stop computation (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). The only tests modified are span-buffer related and do not cover these pagination changes, so the finding about missing tests for this new logic is diff-grounded and actionable, but it’s not itself a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/ — No tests cover the new Lua behavior (eviction above 1000, zunionstore score aggregation with duplicate members, set→zset cutover); the only test changes add end_timestamp_precise literals, so eviction ordering and score handling are unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff materially changes Lua behavior in `add-buffer.lua` (set→zset via `zunionstore`/`zcard`/`zscan` compatibility, introduces eviction logic `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(...) end`, and reduces redirect traversal from 10000→1000). The test diffs shown only add `end_timestamp_precise` fields to existing span fixtures and do not add assertions covering eviction ordering, score semantics/aggregation in `zunionstore`, or the zset cutover behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for new nontrivial logic, not a directly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment claims Cursor now "allows negative offsets" as an optimization, but no functional change was made to the class; it documents behavior that doesn't exist (and negative offsets actually break queryset slicing downstream).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds comments in `Cursor.__init__` claiming support for negative offsets without changing `Cursor` behavior, and it also introduces/retains code paths that can pass negative offsets into Django queryset slicing (e.g., `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` uses `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, and the earlier paginator change still uses `offset` un-clamped when `cursor.is_prev`). Django querysets do not support negative slicing, so this “negative offset” behavior is not actually safe and can break pagination at runtime; thus the comment is misleading and the new/maintained negative-offset slicing is a real defect.
